name: Neurolytic Swarm Dispersal Drone NSD-7 'Locust'
description:
The NSD-7 is a mid-tier autonomous dispersal platform roughly the size of a human fist, housing a compressed micro-swarm of 400–600 semi-independent sub-drones, each no larger than a fingernail. Upon release, the parent chassis identifies thermal signatures within a programmable radius and detonates its swarm canister, sending sub-units in ballistic arcs calibrated to maximize coverage across irregular terrain. Each sub-drone carries a micro-filament electrode array capable of delivering targeted neurolytic pulses to exposed skin or thin fabric.

What distinguishes the NSD-7 from earlier swarm platforms is its use of distributed piezoelectric power harvesting — each sub-drone recharges its discharge capacitor from ambient vibration and pressure as it lands or crawls across a target's body, meaning a single deployment can sustain harassment for up to eighteen minutes without an external power source. The parent drone also maintains a low-frequency coordination signal that prevents sub-units from clustering inefficiently, spreading them in optimized interference patterns across multiple targets simultaneously.

In practice, the NSD-7 does not kill. It overwhelms. Targets experience cascading muscle convulsions, disorientation, and involuntary vocalization as sub-drones fire in coordinated sequences designed to prevent neurological adaptation. Crowd control units favor it for its deniability — sub-drones are difficult to collect as evidence and degrade in UV light within 36 hours.
specifications:
parent chassis dimensions: 11cm x 9cm x 7cm
sub drone count: 400–600 units per canister
sub drone dimensions: 14mm x 8mm
operational duration: Up to 18 minutes per deployment
effective radius: 12m dispersal, 25m harassment range
target capacity: Up to 8 simultaneous targets
UV degradation window: 36 hours
weight: 340g (loaded)
power source: Piezoelectric ambient harvesting per sub-drone; lithium-ceramic primary cell in parent chassis
tactical_use: Operators typically deploy NSD-7 units ahead of advancing forces to soften crowd resistance or flush targets from concealed positions. The drone is released from cover — thrown, dropped from an elevated position, or launched from a standard 40mm compatible tube — and immediately begins autonomous target acquisition. Security teams use them to deny extraction routes, as the sub-drone swarm renders affected areas nearly impassable without full body enclosure. Counter-insurgency operators have been documented using multiple NSD-7 units in overlapping patterns to create sustained area-denial corridors lasting well beyond the initial deployment window.
cultural_context: In GLMZ's lower districts, 'getting Locusted' has entered street vernacular as a term for being overwhelmed by bureaucratic or corporate harassment — too many small problems arriving simultaneously to address any one of them. The NSD-7's civilian reputation is one of humiliation rather than fear; it is the weapon of administrators and enforcers who want compliance without martyrs. Black market operators have begun stripping the neurolytic payloads and repurposing sub-drone chassis for surveillance, a modification known as 'seeding.'
known_users: Arcturus Defense Solutions contracted crowd suppression units
District 7 Municipal Enforcement Bureau (documented field use, officially unacknowledged)
story_hooks: A canister of NSD-7 sub-drones has been seeded throughout a luxury residential tower — someone is watching every resident, and the 36-hour degradation window is already ticking.
A runner claims they were Locusted by units bearing a corporate logo that dissolved before any evidence could be gathered. No one believes them until a second victim surfaces.

The players are hired to retrieve an NSD-7 prototype with an experimental sub-drone that does not degrade — Arcturus wants it back before anyone realizes permanent surveillance swarms are already in the field.
